texts.title: Happy enough?
texts.hook.h1: Try it: tell yourself « I must enjoy today! »
texts.hook.h2: Want to be happy? They say: stop looking for happiness… really?
texts.hook.h3.frame: Waited all year… and felt bad
texts.hook.h3: The day I waited for all year… was the day I felt worst.
texts.hook.h4: 8,331 Dutch people: those who care most about happiness… unhappier or happier?
texts.hook.h5: When did you last ask yourself « am I happy? »
texts.s1.n1: This is Nour, on the company trip.
texts.s1.l1: I have to enjoy every minute!
texts.s1.l2: Am I happy enough?… It should be more!
texts.s1.l3: The sea is amazing, isn't it?
texts.s1.l4: Yes… but not how I imagined.
texts.s1.a2: And you… when you said « I must enjoy it »?
texts.s1.n2: Let's play it again… this time Nour won't measure her joy.
texts.s1.l5: The sea is amazing, isn't it?
texts.s1.l6: Yes, nice… let's go sit with the others.
texts.book.card: Wanting more good feelings… is itself a bad feeling.
texts.book.l1: The book says: the more you chase being happy… the less satisfied you are.
texts.book.l2: Like someone longing to be loved… who feels lonelier.
texts.verdict.card: 8,331 Dutch · valuing happiness: better off · as it grew: joy and distress
texts.verdict.nuance: Those who worry about their happiness are worse off… those who seek it with others, more satisfied.
texts.verdict.l2: 8,331 Dutch people: those who care about happiness are, on average, better off.
texts.takeaway.l1: Try it like Nour: instead of measuring your joy… sit with your loved ones. It may help.
texts.takeaway.orientation: If the distress lasts for weeks and affects your life, talk to a psychologist.
texts.share: Send this to someone waiting for the perfect day.
texts.verdict.l3: But in one experiment, people who read an article praising happiness… enjoyed a nice film less.
